claims.text: The composition is changed from Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 to Fe22Ni16Co19Mn12Cr16P15.
The modified alloy is processed by melt spinning on a copper wheel at 40 m/s.
Increasing Fe and Co while reducing Mn and P will shift solidification toward a eutectic-dominated path.
The modified composition and rapid melt spinning will suppress primary crystallization.
Melt spinning the modified alloy at 40 m/s will produce a fully amorphous structure.
The modified, melt-spun alloy will have enhanced thermal stability.
The modified alloy was prepared from elemental powders with at least 99.9 wt.% purity by arc melting and was remelted at least six times.
The modified alloy is available as slower-cooled arc-melted ingots and approximately 20 μm melt-spun ribbons.
Cooling of the arc-melted ingot begins near 1459 K at an average cooling rate of approximately 95.9 K/s.
DSC heating and cooling are performed in argon at 20 K/min.
The intervention produces fine, rod-like eutectic colonies in rapidly quenched samples.
The eutectic-dominated structure minimizes elemental segregation.
The eutectic-dominated structure suppresses early phosphide nucleation.
Increasing Fe and Co while reducing Mn and P decreases the tendency for primary solid-solution crystallization.
Increasing Fe and Co while reducing Mn and P decreases high-temperature phosphide formation.
Cooperative eutectic growth suppresses elemental partitioning and hinders nucleation of unwanted phases.
Relative to Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20, the modified alloy will exhibit a simpler, predominantly eutectic crystallization sequence and a larger eutectic fraction.
The modified melt-spun alloy will exhibit a broader crystallization interval during DSC reheating.
The baseline Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 alloy exhibits extensive primary and non-eutectic crystallization with multiple solidification arrests, especially under slower cooling.
The predicted amorphous retention is limited primarily to approximately 20 μm ribbons produced at 40 m/s and may not occur in bulk or at substantially lower cooling rates.

contradictions.description: The rapidly quenched product is described both as containing fine, rod-like eutectic colonies or a larger eutectic fraction and as being fully amorphous. Crystalline eutectic colonies cannot simultaneously constitute a fully amorphous as-quenched structure unless the eutectic description refers only to a later devitrified state, which is not stated.
